title: Quantum Markov Chains for an Asymmetric Mixed Ising-XY Model on a Cayley Tree
abstract: We study a mixed quantum Ising-$XY$ model on the semi-infinite rooted Cayley tree of order two. For every vertex $u$, the edge $\langle u,(u,1)\rangle$ carries an $XY$ interaction and the edge $\langle u,(u,2)\rangle$ carries an Ising interaction. Using the compatibility criterion for tree-indexed quantum Markov chains and consistently working with the normalized trace, we derive the translation-invariant boundary equation and compute explicitly the associated local transfer operator, namely the one-step partial-trace map which propagates successor boundary data to the parent vertex. We prove that the boundary equation has a unique positive translation-invariant solution for all $J_I,J_{XY}\in\mathbb R$ and $β>0$. Hence the model admits a unique translation-invariant quantum Markov chain generated by a positive translation-invariant boundary condition. We also show that the reduced boundary-law dynamics, i.e. the induced finite-dimensional recursion for the boundary-law parameters, has no admissible periodic points of period greater than one and compute the local two-site entanglement on the natural three-site cluster of the tree.
summary: This paper rigorously analyzes the quantum dynamics of a mixed Ising-XY model situated on an infinite Cayley tree. By utilizing Quantum Markov Chain theory, the authors prove that the system admits a unique translation-invariant steady state solution. This establishes strong mathematical constraints on the possible physical states achievable by this complex interacting spin system.
main_problem: The study investigates Quantum Markov Chains (QMC) associated with a mixed Ising-XY model defined on an infinite Cayley tree structure.
main_result: The paper proves the existence and uniqueness of a translation-invariant QMC solution for all coupling constants, alongside demonstrating that the reduced dynamics possess no periodic points beyond period one.
method: The analysis employs the compatibility criterion for tree-indexed QMCs, deriving boundary equations solved via transfer operators and analyzing the resulting finite-dimensional dynamical system.
model_or_system: The model is a mixed Ising-XY Hamiltonian defined on the semi-infinite rooted Cayley tree of order two. The interactions are locally asymmetric: XY coupling acts along one branch, and Ising coupling acts along the other.
key_observables: Local two-site entanglement; the boundary law parameters (Bloch coefficients); existence/uniqueness of translation-invariant solutions.
important_parameters: Coupling strengths ($J_I, J_{XY}$), inverse temperature ($ eta$), and the structure of the tree ($\Gamma_2^+$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on working with the normalized trace convention and assuming the existence of a unique positive translation-invariant solution to proceed.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the locally asymmetric mixed Ising–XY assignment (XY on one edge, Ising on the other) on the Cayley Tree. Figure 2 shows the local three-site interaction block at a vertex.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the QMC framework using compatibility criteria, derives the boundary equation and transfer operator, analyzes the resulting reduced dynamical system for periodic points, proves uniqueness theorems for the translation-invariant solution, and concludes with entanglement calculations.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous mathematical tools (QMCs) to characterize equilibrium states in complex quantum spin systems on infinite lattices, which is crucial for understanding critical phenomena and phase transitions in condensed matter theory.
